newsitem.title: USA: NYC eyes plan to back debt with late parking fines.
newsitem.headline: NYC eyes plan to back debt with late parking fines.

text.p: New York City again is weighing a plan to back debt with overdue parking tickets, city officials said on Friday.
But officials added that the proposal, though in the fiscal 1998 budget plan, was preliminary.

Adam Barsky, first deputy commissioner of the city's Finance Department, when asked how big any such asset-backed bond sale might be, replied: "We're looking at somewhere in the neighborhood of $40 to $50 million."
Saying there still were a number of legal and structural issues that had to be worked out, he explained that the debt would be backed with parking tickets that had not been paid for over one year.

A city source, who declined to be named, said that New York City, which is flush with tax revenues thanks to Wall Street's big profits, had no pressing need for this offering. "It's in my back pocket," he said.
New York City last year weighed selling its overdue parking fines to a private entity that would use the revenues to back the new debt, but no action was taken.
